# Code Map — Budgeting (Zero-Based Budgeting Console)

Next.js 16 / React 19, Owner/Accountant only. The design system (ui/, theme.ts,
globals.css, NavRail, HeaderClock) is a **verbatim copy of Dispatcher** — change Dispatcher
first, then re-copy; never edit the copy in place. Manifest + drift check: Budgeting/CLAUDE.md.

<!-- notes:budgeting-screens:start -->
- Every period-scoped screen (lib/nav.ts PERIOD_SCOPED — all but Vendors, Cost Centres, QuickBooks and Settings) renders screens/periods/PeriodChooser until a period is entered (lib/workingPeriod.ts, sessionStorage); PeriodBanner's SWITCH PERIOD is the only way out, blocked while lib/periodHold.ts holds a request.
- BudgetPeriods.tsx is only a host for periods/PeriodDashboard (LifecycleStepper, PlanningChecklist, PriorityBreakdown, CostCentreBreakdown, VendorBreakdown, CopyFromPeriodPanel, one AllocationSection per code category). Headline tiles and the vendor/cost-centre panels are the server's rollups; the by-priority breakdown is summed client-side.
- A period is planned in exactly one place, the dashboard: the flat Allocations screen was deleted rather than fixed, so don't re-add a second entry point (the reasoning is in lib/nav.ts).
- Budget codes belong to a period (each period has its own chart); screens/codes/CopyCodesPanel copies a chart from another period. Vendors and CostCentres are tenant-wide registers with their own screens (master/detail, not tabs on Budget Codes).
- After a transition, item save/removal or copy, the UI polls with refetchUntil (stateAfter / itemReflects predicates) before refreshing the period list — reads are eventually consistent.
<!-- notes:budgeting-screens:end -->

<!-- gen:budgeting-components:end -->
<!-- notes:budgeting-components:start -->
- RoleGate enforces the Owner/Accountant client-side gate (UX only — the security boundary is the gateway BudgetAccess policy on /api/budgeting).
- BudgetItemFormModal adds/edits one budget item (cost build-up, priority, recurrence, spend type) — the planning unit since items replaced one set figure per code; on the wire it is still an allocation (/periods/{id}/allocations). Expense items name vendors through VendorSharesEditor (dollar shares summing exactly to the amount); revenue items keep a free-text payer.
- QboCallback is the body of app/qbo/callback, Intuit's OAuth redirect target (the API is never public): it strips the one-time code from the address bar, relays it to POST /api/budgeting/qbo/connection/complete as the signed-in user, then lands the console on QuickBooks via lib/landing.ts. No token ever reaches the browser.
<!-- notes:budgeting-components:end -->

## Lib — Budgeting/lib (40 files)
<!-- gen:budgeting-lib:start -->
api/ (13): budgeting, budgeting.requests.test, budgeting.test, costCentres.requests.test, format, identity, identity.test, qbo, qbo.requests.test, qbo.test, shared, transport, transport.test
Top-level: accessSeam.test, auth, claims.test, claims, clipboard, costCentres.test, costCentres, data, format, landing, legal, money.test, money, nav, period, periodHold, roles.test, roles, theme, types, useToday, vendorShares.test, vendorShares, vendors.test, vendors, workingPeriod.test, workingPeriod
<!-- gen:budgeting-lib:end -->
<!-- notes:budgeting-lib:start -->
- api/budgeting.ts is the real API wiring — periods, per-period codes (/periods/{id}/codes), budget items (/periods/{id}/allocations), the vendor and cost-centre registers and the period rollups all come from the backend; data.ts keeps only the mock actuals/variance (plus a budgetCodes lookup feeding those mock rows). api/qbo.ts is separate because the QuickBooks connection is tenant-wide, never under a period.
- api/identity.ts is the one client here that calls a non-budgeting endpoint (Identity's /api/identity/auth/profile, feeding components/ProfileForm.tsx in the Settings Profile tab); its PUT sends the whole profile, so an omitted field clears rather than preserves.
- vendors.ts, vendorShares.ts and costCentres.ts are pure client mirrors of the server's register rules, each pinned to the C# it copies by its own test — the server re-checks and wins. landing.ts is a one-shot sessionStorage "open this screen next" hint, used only by the QBO callback (the console has no URL routing).
<!-- notes:budgeting-lib:end -->
